article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 80% Indica / 20% Sativa
Genetics: Gelato Sorbet × Lava Cake
Breeder: DNA Genetics
THC Content: 23-26%
CBD Content: Typically low
Terpene Profile: Myrcene dominant
Primary Flavors: Vanilla frosting, sweet cream, cake, fruit
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: 340–400 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 18 oz. per plant
Grow Difficulty: Easy

DNA Cake is a dessert strain in the literal sense of the word. Freshly opened flowers can smell like vanilla frosting, sweet cream, baked cake, and ripe fruit before a darker mixture of spice, earth, and diesel emerges underneath. DNA Genetics created the cultivar by crossing Gelato Sorbet with Lava Cake, bringing several of modern cannabis breeding’s most recognizable dessert families into one heavily indica-dominant plant. The flower looks the part as well, developing dense resinous buds that can carry purple and green coloration beneath a thick coat of trichomes.

Yet the strain is not simply another sweet variety built around a fashionable name. Its effects move from cheerful cerebral euphoria into increasingly deep physical relaxation, while its cultivation profile remains practical enough for relatively inexperienced growers. Plants stay bushy, generally finish flowering within eight to nine weeks, and respond well to straightforward canopy management. The combination of creamy flavor, substantial resin production, manageable structure, and a relaxing finish makes DNA Cake particularly representative of the modern dessert-style marijuana category.
Genetics and Lineage

DNA Genetics confirms DNA Cake as Gelato Sorbet × Lava Cake. Gelato Sorbet is itself a cross of Gelato #33 and Sorbet, linking the cultivar to the Gelato family that developed from Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint Cookies ancestry. Gelato #33 contributes dense resinous flower, creamy sweetness, fruit, color, and substantial potency, while the proprietary Sorbet side adds another layer of soft fruit, dessert flavor, and visually attractive flower. Together, those genetics establish the smoother and more confectionary half of DNA Cake.

Lava Cake provides a heavier foundation. The cultivar comes from Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies × Grape Pie , joining Cookies-family sweetness and minty earth with the dark fruit, purple coloration, and resin production associated with Grape Pie. Thin Mint Cookies contributes dense flower, strong trichome coverage, earth, herbs, and a cooling dessert quality, while Grape Pie introduces richer berry and grape characteristics. Lava Cake became especially valued for combining impressive bag appeal with a powerful body-oriented experience.

The final cross concentrates Cookies, Gelato, Grape Pie, and dessert-family traits without completely erasing the gas and earth beneath them. DNA Cake therefore carries cream and vanilla at the surface while retaining enough spice, wood, pine, and diesel to prevent the aroma from becoming one-dimensional. DNA Genetics classifies the strain at roughly 80% indica and 20% sativa, a ratio reflected in its bushy plant structure, dense flowers, and increasingly relaxing effects.
Effects and Experience

The first stage tends to feel brighter than the cultivar’s indica-heavy genetics might suggest. A moderate amount can produce a quick improvement in mood accompanied by euphoria, mental engagement, and a pleasantly focused sensation. Creative hobbies, music, conversation, movies, or other low-pressure activities may feel especially enjoyable during this period because the consumer remains mentally present rather than immediately becoming physically heavy.

That lighter beginning gradually gives way to a much calmer body experience. Muscles relax, movement feels less necessary, and the cerebral energy softens into a more tranquil state. With a moderate serving, the effect can remain relaxing without becoming fully sedating, but larger doses tend to increase heaviness considerably. The later stages may bring sleepiness, appetite stimulation, and a strong desire to settle into a comfortable environment.

DNA Genetics describes the strain as moderate to high in THC rather than assigning one universal percentage to the seed line. That is appropriate because potency can differ substantially between phenotypes and growing environments. Consumers with limited tolerance should therefore approach well-grown flower conservatively. Excessive intake may produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, mental fog, or temporary anxiety before the stronger physical relaxation develops.
Medical Benefits

The progression from euphoria into body calm may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want a cultivar capable of serving different purposes depending on dosage. During the earlier phase, the brighter mental shift may make stress, emotional fatigue, or low mood feel less dominant. At the same time, the experience usually remains calm enough that it does not feel as sharp or restless as highly stimulating sativa weed.

As the physical effects strengthen, general muscular tension and discomfort may become less intrusive. Larger servings can also encourage appetite and drowsiness, making the strain more naturally suited to evening use for many consumers. High-THC marijuana does not affect everyone in the same way, however, and people who are sensitive to intoxication may experience anxiety or uncomfortable mental heaviness if the dose becomes excessive.

Myrcene is identified by DNA Genetics as the dominant terpene and contributes to the woody, spicy, pine-like depth beneath the cultivar’s sweeter aroma. The complete terpene composition can vary between plants, so medical decisions should be based on the actual batch whenever laboratory testing is available. Cannabinoid strength, medications, tolerance, and previous response to cannabis remain more important than assuming every DNA Cake flower will produce identical effects.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Vanilla frosting and sweet cream form the unmistakable opening. The bouquet can resemble cake batter or freshly baked dessert, with a sugary richness that becomes especially strong in properly cured flower. Sweet fruit appears behind the cream during the earlier stages of flowering, adding a softer layer before this marijuana strain develops its heavier mature aroma.

Gas and spice become more obvious at harvest. Breaking apart dense buds releases a danker diesel fragrance accompanied by wood, pine, and a subtle peppery edge. Myrcene contributes to the earthy and forest-like character, giving the finished flower more depth than a purely sugary strain. Some phenotypes may stay heavily dessert oriented, while others reveal a stronger balance between sweet cream and pungent fuel.

On the palate, creamy sweetness generally arrives first, followed by vanilla frosting and mild fruit. Spice and diesel become stronger through the exhale, leaving a deeper finish after the initial dessert notes fade. Vaporization can preserve more of the creamy and fruity character, while combustion tends to emphasize gas, wood, and spice. A patient dry and cure help keep these contrasting layers distinct.
Growing Information

DNA Cake is considered easy enough for newer growers while still offering enough quality to interest experienced cultivators. Plants grow in a compact, bushy pattern consistent with their 80% indica background and typically reach around 90–120 cm indoors. Outdoor specimens can approach approximately 180 cm under favorable conditions. Regular pruning helps open the interior canopy, while low-stress training can spread the main branches horizontally and improve light penetration.

Indoor flowering takes approximately eight to nine weeks. DNA Genetics lists yields around 12–14 oz./m², or roughly 340–400 g/m². The flowers become dense, resinous, and heavily coated with trichomes, giving the cultivar value for rosin and other concentrates in addition to dried flower. Sea of Green cultivation can work particularly well because the relatively compact plants allow growers to create an even canopy without excessive vertical stretch. Experienced cultivators may also use topping, fimming, or supercropping where additional branching is desired.

Outdoor plants can produce up to approximately 18 ounces per plant under favorable conditions and perform best in warm, Mediterranean-like environments. DNA Genetics recommends consistent temperatures and moderate humidity, with 50–60% relative humidity during much of the cycle and lower moisture levels as dense flowers mature. Good airflow becomes increasingly important near harvest because the bushy plant structure can trap humidity around the buds. In Northern Hemisphere gardens, maturity generally falls during October depending on latitude and flowering onset.
FAQ
What strains make DNA Cake?
DNA Cake was bred by DNA Genetics from Gelato Sorbet × Lava Cake. Gelato Sorbet comes from Gelato #33 × Sorbet, while Lava Cake combines Thin Mint Girl Scout Cookies with Grape Pie.
Is DNA Cake indica or sativa?
DNA Genetics classifies DNA Cake at approximately 80% indica and 20% sativa. Its bushy structure, dense buds, and strong later-stage physical relaxation all reflect the dominant indica influence.
What does DNA Cake taste like?
The primary flavors include vanilla frosting, sweet cream, cake, fruit, spice, pine, and diesel. Sweet dessert notes lead the profile, while gas and spice become more noticeable toward the finish.
How long does DNA Cake take to flower?
DNA Cake typically flowers for approximately eight to nine weeks indoors. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity during October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Is DNA Cake easy to grow?

Yes. DNA Genetics describes the cultivar as beginner friendly. Plants remain relatively compact, respond well to low-stress training and Sea of Green cultivation, and can produce dense resinous flowers without requiring an unusually complicated grow routine.
Final Thoughts on DNA Cake

DNA Cake brings together several influential dessert families without losing the deeper cannabis character beneath the sweetness. Gelato Sorbet contributes cream, fruit, color, and the polished flower structure associated with Gelato genetics, while Lava Cake adds Cookies, Grape Pie, resin, and a heavier physical personality. The result tastes unmistakably dessert inspired but still carries enough diesel, pine, spice, and earth to remain complex.

Cultivation is equally straightforward. An eight-to-nine-week flowering period, compact bushy structure, indoor yields around 340–400 g/m², and outdoor production reaching roughly 510 grams per plant give the cultivar practical value beyond its name and bag appeal. Dense trichome development also makes properly selected plants useful for concentrate production.

For consumers, the experience moves in a clear direction: euphoria and cheerful mental engagement arrive first, physical relaxation builds afterward, and larger servings can eventually become quite sleepy. Combined with vanilla frosting, cream, fruit, spice, and gas, that progression gives DNA Cake a well-rounded identity within the modern dessert marijuana category. It is a cultivar built around sweetness, but its Kush, Cookies, and Grape Pie influence give it enough depth to offer considerably more than flavor alone.
